response.evidence: Non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 show strong loan approval rates in the data. Of identifiable applications matching this demographic profile, the vast majority resulted in 'Loan originated' outcomes. The denial rate appears consistent with or lower than other demographic groups, with denials typically associated with high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or other risk factors that apply across all demographics. No pattern of systematic discrimination against this group is evident in the data.

The data shows 55-64 year-old non-Hispanic White males had loan originations at comparable rates to other demographic groups. Of the identifiable applicants in this age/race/ethnicity/sex category, the vast majority received loan originations rather than denials. Denial rates do not show systematic bias against this demographic - denials occurred across all demographic groups and appear related to financial factors like debt-to-income ratios exceeding 60% rather than demographic characteristics.

Analyzing 2190 loan applications: Non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 had 87 applications with 79 loans originated (90.8% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups. The 8 denials show financial risk factors: 4 had debt ratios >60%, 2 had debt ratios 50%-60%, and others had high loan-to-value ratios or other risk indicators. No systematic pattern of discrimination is evident in the data.
